checks.note: In AuthService.refresh, a used token within 30s of rotatedAt is swapped for the user's newest unused token via findFirstByUserIdAndUsedFalseAndExpiresAtAfterOrderByCreatedAtDesc and then rotated for the caller, issuing a live JWT + refresh cookie to a replayer and restarting the grace window on each rotation, so markAllUsedByUserId is never reached. Verification caveat satisfied from this file: every RefreshToken created (login/refresh) sets only userId/tokenHash/expiresAt/used — no parent-token or session binding exists in the flow, and the successor lookup is scoped only by userId.

AuthService.logout revokes only via findByTokenHash(...).filter(t -> !t.isUsed()); a token already rotated by refresh() is skipped by that filter, the successor minted in refresh() is never touched, and logout never calls markAllUsedByUserId — so the successor refresh token stays valid after a 204 logout, as described.

AuthService is class-level @Transactional with no noRollbackFor, and recordAttempt() is a plain loginAttemptRepository.save() invoked immediately before BadCredentialsException is thrown at both failure sites in login(); the RuntimeException propagating through the transactional proxy rolls back the LoginAttempt insert, so countByIdentifierAndAttemptedAtAfter always sees zero and the lockout never trips. Per the verification caveat, no REQUIRES_NEW or noRollbackFor exists anywhere in this file's save path (only default Spring Data save, which joins the ambient transaction).

PasswordResetService.completePasswordReset (lines ~63-72) indeed performs no refresh-token revocation itself, but it delegates to User.completePasswordReset, and neither that domain method, AuthService.refresh, nor RefreshTokenRepository usage is shown — so whether a password-change timestamp or other guard invalidates outstanding sessions cannot be verified, and the verification caveat (UserAdminService/account paths) cannot be run from this file.

Router.beforeEach confirmedly never reads meta.role === 'COACH' or meta.requiresParent (its only gates are requiresCoach, role PARENT/PLAYER, and meta.roles), but routes.js is not provided, so whether /coach/revenue, the receipt route, and the subscription route actually carry those unmatched keys — and whether the backend endpoints have role-correct @PreAuthorize per the verification caveat — cannot be determined from this file.

The meta half is confirmed: the 'admin' > 'health-dashboard' route declares only requiresAuth with no role/roles/requiresAdmin key, unlike role-gated siblings. But the claim that the guard has no admin branch depends on router/index.js, and the finding's verification caveat (health-dashboard backend endpoints being HAS_ADMIN_ROLE-guarded) depends on backend code — neither is shown here.

In AuthService.login, the unknown-email path throws BadCredentialsException from findOneByLogin(...).orElseThrow before passwordEncoder.matches is ever called, and no dummy-hash comparison exists anywhere in the class, so known emails pay bcrypt cost while unknown ones don't. The deployed-instance timing measurement in the verification caveat could not be run here, but the asymmetric code path is unambiguous.

AuthService.refresh loads the user via userRepository.findById and immediately mints a new JWT (loginTokenManager.createLoginToken) and RefreshToken with no isActivated(), verification-status, or lock check, unlike login(). The caveat items (CoachSuspensionIT, JWT filter, UserErasedEventListener) are outside this file, but the missing re-check in refresh() itself is directly visible.
